topic.source_contract: TfL PTAL and London Plan public-transport accessibility evidence

sources.publisher: Transport for London via London Datastore

facts.scope_guard: PTAL measures network-access density at a point and is not full journey quality, capacity, title or planning entitlement.
Policy use of PTAL does not convert a grid score into automatic parking, density or permission entitlement.

facts.density_context: connectivity and accessibility by walking, cycling and public transport including PTAL and local services
facts.scope_guard: Connectivity is one component and planned infrastructure must be evidenced; PTAL alone is not density capacity.

facts.site_context: existing or planned PTAL and station or town-centre proximity may inform housing opportunity
facts.scope_guard: Strategic opportunity criteria are not candidate-specific permission, capacity or delivery proof.

scope_guards: PTAL measures access density to public transport and is not a complete journey-quality measure.
PTAL excludes speed, utility, crowding and ease of interchange.
Historic 2015 files are not silently treated as current WebCAT values.
A 100-metre grid value is not an HMLR title, site boundary or application red-line.
PTAL does not establish legal vehicular or pedestrian access rights.
London Plan use of PTAL does not create automatic density, parking or permission entitlement.
Planned public-transport service is not treated as delivered capacity without commitment and timing evidence.
No score or promotion is written without exact point, current PTAL, wider connectivity, planning and title evidence.
